rgb: The camera wearer is positioned roughly 0.5 to 0.8 m before an L-shaped wooden reception counter, with its front portion running left-to-right and then extending backward beside a long hallway that continues more than 10 m into the right background; a white pillar carrying fire extinguishers and a wooden lattice screen stand 2.5 to 3 m behind the desk. From left to right on the countertop, 0.5 to 1.8 m from the camera wearer, are a beige-and-brown handbag (on the left and within arm's reach), a small sign, a black monitor facing away from the viewer, a telephone, a receipt printer, a card terminal, a clipboard, and a clear spray bottle. About 1.2 to 1.5 m in front of the camera wearer, a woman wearing a white shirt sits behind the counter, with the desk and monitor obscuring her from the waist down; in frame 1 she bends forward with her hands at the printer, in frames 2 through 4 she sits upright facing the counter while angled and looking slightly toward the desk's right side, and in frame 5 she is largely cut off at the left edge. Directly to the camera wearer's left (~0.5 to 0.8 m away and ~1.2 m from the seated woman), a person with a dark purple sleeve has both hands inside the open handbag in frame 1 while most of their body remains unseen, vanishes beyond the left border in frames 2 and 5, and is represented only by an arm and the handbag along the left edge in frames 3 and 4. In frames 2 to 4, an extended left hand holding a small card appears at the bottom-right edge around 0.6 m away; in frame 5, the camera rotates rightward, moving the desk's left side out of sight and exposing a red-shirted person standing 0.7 to 1.0 m to the right (~1.5 to 2.0 m from the woman behind the desk), facing the counter and looking at the camera wearer while holding the card above the counter corner within arm's reach.
depth: The depth map represents the reception area's continuous 3D structure, with a wooden counter occupying the immediate foreground at 0.3 to 1.2 m and receding beside a long corridor on the right that reaches more than 5 m into the dark background. In frames 1 through 4, a person accompanied by a handbag stands at the far left, 0.4 to 0.7 m away, and is partly cropped from view in frames 2 to 4; meanwhile, a receptionist sits behind the counter approximately 1.2 to 1.5 m ahead of the camera wearer and about 1.0 to 1.2 m right of the left person, facing forward toward the counter and camera wearer from behind a monitor, telephone, and receipt printer that obscure part of their lower torso. A hand enters the lower-right foreground at 0.4 to 0.6 m in frames 2 to 4, and when the camera wearer turns rightward in frame 5, the receptionist moves to the extreme left edge as the red-shirted person on the right comes into view 0.6 to 0.9 m away (roughly 1.5 m from the receptionist), facing and looking at the camera wearer with their right hand placed on the counter edge. Near-white values indicate that the counter's front edge, the left-side handbag, and the extended hand of the person on the right lie within the camera wearer's arm's reach (under 0.8 m), while the monitor, printer, and clipboard are reachable by the receptionist. Compared with the RGB image alone, this map reveals the gradual distance change across the countertop and corridor wall much more clearly, although it performs poorly on thin or transparent items such as the counter's spray bottle, which merges into the background depth, and reduces subtle facial and hand contours to flat, uniform silhouettes.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map separates individual foreground entities from the unlabelled counter and hallway, locating the person and handbag at the far left (0.4 to 0.7 m away), the seated receptionist at center-left (1.2 to 1.5 m away and facing the camera wearer), the objects on the counter before the receptionist, and the right-side person (0.5 to 0.9 m away and around 1.5 m from the receptionist), who faces and looks at the camera wearer in frame 5. The receptionist appears behind and slightly higher than the counter equipment (labelled 'laptop') and left of the clipboard (labelled 'book'); the counter and equipment hide the receptionist's lower half, while the person on the left is partly outside the left frame boundary in frames 1, 3, and 4 and entirely absent from view in frames 2 and 5. Throughout the five frames, the masks follow the camera wearer's rightward pan, first depicting the right-side person only as a cropped hand and arm in the lower-right corner of frames 2 and 3 (within 0.6 m and inside the camera wearer's arm's reach), then exposing their complete upper body in frame 5 along with a card (labelled 'remote') reachable by both that person and the camera wearer. Although the masks distinguish intersecting silhouettes—such as the receptionist's torso behind the monitor and the left person's body beside the handbag—more clearly than unprocessed RGB textures, their semantic labelling and frame-to-frame consistency are unreliable. In particular, the system labels the desktop monitor and telephone as 'laptop', the clipboard as 'book', the card as 'remote', the frame-4 handbag as part of a 'person', the wooden lattice screen above the receptionist in frame 4 as a 'tv', and the frame-5 spray bottle as both a 'person' and 'book'; it also fails to detect the receptionist at all in frame 4.
pose: The body-and-hand skeleton map follows sparse 2D joint landmarks and limb directions throughout the reception area, identifying the receptionist's left hand on the counter in frame 1 (approximately 1.2 m away), the receptionist's upper-body skeleton behind the counter in frames 2 and 3 (1.2 to 1.5 m away), a close hand at the lower-right corner in frame 2 (around 0.5 m away), and the right-side person's upper body, facial landmarks, and right hand in frame 5 (0.6 to 0.9 m away). During frames 2 and 3, vectors from the receptionist's shoulders and arms point forward and downward toward the countertop within their arm's reach, while the counter and monitor block their lower body. By frame 5, after the camera wearer turns right, the receptionist has moved beyond the tracked region on the left, whereas the person on the right stands 0.6 to 0.9 m in front of the camera wearer (approximately 1.5 m from the receptionist's location); balanced shoulder keypoints and centrally aligned facial keypoints establish that their head and torso face straight toward the camera wearer, as their right arm reaches forward and downward to set their magenta-mapped hand on the counter within both their own and the camera wearer's arm's reach. The clearly drawn finger and limb segments make precise hand configuration and shoulder direction quicker to interpret than in the motion-blurred RGB imagery. Nevertheless, the map's coverage and stability are very unreliable: it never detects the far-left person in any frame, omits the receptionist's skeleton completely in frames 1, 4, and 5, fails to capture the lower-right hand in frames 3 and 4, and renders the receptionist's shoulder-and-head structure in frames 2 and 3 as distorted and collapsed.
